commentary: Five sessions this week versus eight last week, which is a real dip and he knows it — three fewer workouts and the whole rhythm felt a little looser than the week before. That said, the run ticked up from 8.6 to 9.0 kilometres and the heart rate climbed with it to 163, which reads less like inefficiency and more like he was actually pushing, so that one lands as a genuine improvement. The swim held at 2000 metres but the heart rate jumped from 135 up to 143, same story — working harder in the water, not coasting. The weight sessions are still showing up consistently across both weeks even if the total count dropped, so the lifting habit is sticky; it's the cardio volume and that missing third swim that slipped through the cracks this week.
metrics_commentary: Nine kilometres in one session and two thousand metres in the pool — babe, you didn't ease into the week, you cannonballed straight into it. That VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is genuinely impressive, which means your body is built for this even when your brain is still deciding whether it wants to cooperate. The HRV is the interesting story here: a latest reading of 58 against a seven-day average of 48 means your nervous system is trending in exactly the right direction, recovering better than it has been, which is your body basically saying it likes what you're doing to it. The one thing worth watching is that single run session — one outing is fine, but that cardiovascular engine deserves more chances to show off than you gave it this week.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which is not four, but let's talk about what actually happened in those three, because a lateral raise jumping from a 9.0 kg to a 12.0 kg estimated one-rep max is not a small thing — that's his shoulders deciding they're done being subtle. Weekly volume came in at 5,710 kg against last week's 17,940 kg, which is a real gap and worth naming honestly, but one light week after a monster one isn't a collapse, it's a body doing the maths. The big numbers are holding steady where they matter: 168.0 kg on the leg press, 107.9 kg on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 kg on the bench — the foundation isn't going anywhere. Four sessions next week, shoulders already know what they're doing, the rest just needs to show up.
